description:
FOUND s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) by the FAILURE-EXPERIENCE battery (Q5; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q5/run.pl, cases/, run1.log: 30 scenarios under perl and under the user-facing `pcl`; compared = exit status, stdout, stderr LINE COUNT, Lisp leaking).  The battery's good news first: 17 of 30 scenarios are perl-shaped to the byte or nearly (string die with and without newline, die 3 frames deep, die with $! as status, exit N, warn, BEGIN die, rethrow, utf8 die text, die in a sort comparator, the line number in a die message) -- #1247(b)'s uncaught-die hook did its job.  What is left:

(a) OBJECT DIE.  cases/03-die-hashref.pl `die { code => 42 };` and cases/04-die-object-str.pl (a class with `use overload q{""}`):
        perl:  HASH(0x5af562a943b8)          /   E: custom failure                  (1 line, rc 255)
        pcl :  #S(p-box\n   :value #<hash-table :TEST equal :COUNT 1 {12019A96B3}>\n   :nv nil ... :is-ref nil)   (8 lines, rc 255)
    MECHANISM (read): `%p-uncaught-die-hook` prints `(princ-to-string condition)`; for a `p-exception` that is the condition's report = the raw payload printed by the Lisp printer.  FIX: print `(to-string PAYLOAD)` -- the ordinary perl stringification (it runs the `""` overload, prints `CLASS=HASH(0x..)` for a plain object); perl appends nothing for a reference payload.  Exception OBJECTS are how modern Perl dies (Exception::Class, Throwable, Moo-based errors, `die My::Err->new(...)`), so an uncaught one is an everyday sight.  Probe also: an object whose `""` handler itself dies; `die [1,2]`; a payload that is a code ref; `PROPAGATE`.
(b) PERL FATALS RAISED AS PLAIN CL ERRORS.  cases/08-method-on-undef.pl `my $o; $o->foo;` and cases/23-not-code-ref.pl `my $g = {}; $g->();`:
        perl:  Can't call method "foo" on an undefined value at FILE line 1.      (1 line, rc 255)
        pcl :  Unhandled simple-error in thread #<sb-thread:thread tid=... "main thread" running {...}>: Can't call method foo on an undefined value + Backtrace, 30 lines, rc 1
    Both are CATCHABLE today (`eval { $o->m }` sets $@ -- probed), so only the UNCAUGHT path is wrong.  MECHANISM (read): the hook's classifier `%p-perl-die-p` = p-exception or p-die-error, "everything else reaching the debugger is a PCL bug" -- but cl/pcl-runtime.lisp has 91 plain `(error "...")` sites against 52 `(p-die ...)`, and an unknown share of the 91 are PERL'S diagnostics (perldiag texts), not PCL bugs.  FIX = an AUDIT, not a blanket: walk the 91 sites; a site whose message is a perl run-time fatal raises through `%p-die-error` (then the hook, the exit status and -- when #1240's line register is on -- the location all follow for free); a site that really is an internal invariant stays loud.  DESIGN QUESTION FOR THE USER (small): should an internal error ALSO be one line by default -- `PCL internal error: <text> (PCL_BACKTRACE=1 for the Lisp backtrace)` -- with the backtrace behind an env switch?  The test runners want the backtrace (set the switch in tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm); a user never does.
    Same family, already owned elsewhere: the message TEXT drops perl's quotes (`method foo` vs `method "foo"`) -- fix at the same site, it is free there.
NOT NEW, measured again by the battery (owners): the "While evaluating the form starting at line N ... of #P..." context line on a source load = #1595 / #1970 (seen here on `pcl -e 'die "x\n"'` = 2 lines, and on a missing module); `$SIG{__DIE__}` never invoked = #1554; deep recursion = 1012 stderr lines (#1929); strict refs / strict vars / read-only modification not enforced = the Q3 family (#2103); `use warnings` uninitialized = #221.
BAR: the q5 battery before -> after (errC = errP and rc equal for cases 03 04 08 23), a Pl/t guard file that runs the four shapes through the stderr-aware helper (#355) and asserts ONE stderr line + status 255; companion op/die.t op/die_exit.t op/die_keeperr.t lib/croak.t by rows; full sweep (cl/ change).
SIZE: (a) is an hour; (b)'s audit is half an agent-day.  Filler-rule sized; no design beyond the USER question.


=== USER RULING s494 (2026-09-21) -- the question inside this task is ANSWERED ===
USER, s494 (2026-09-21): "It is OK if errors aren't the same as Perl, as long as they fail in the same places. But we don't want it to be horribly messy either. :-)"
SO: (1) message TEXT is not the bar (it never was: project_error_message_fidelity_not_required) -- do NOT chase perl's wording in the 91-site audit; (2) WHERE a program fails IS the bar: an uncaught error must end the program at the statement perl ends it, with a non-zero status; (3) TIDY is a bar too: **an uncaught error of ANY kind -- perl-level or PCL-internal -- is ONE readable line on stderr (+ the location when the line register is on), never a 30-line SBCL backtrace and never a box struct**; the backtrace moves behind `PCL_BACKTRACE=1`, which the TEST RUNNERS set in the one command-line builder (tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm) so crash forensics keep working.  The internal-error line should say it is PCL's fault and how to get the backtrace: `PCL internal error: <text> (set PCL_BACKTRACE=1 for the Lisp backtrace)`.  The audit shrinks accordingly: its job is no longer to re-class 91 sites one by one but to make the TOP-LEVEL HOOK tidy for everything, and then to check that the perl-visible fatals exit 255 (perl's status) rather than 1.  Same ruling covers #1595 / #1970's load-context line and #1929's 1012 lines: they are MESS, in scope of `tidy`.

=== HALF DONE (s494g, 2026-09-25, Opus) -- (a) and the (b) audit SHIPPED; the USER's internal-error half is OPEN ===
(a) %p-uncaught-die-hook prints %p-uncaught-die-text: a p-exception's payload through to-string (the "" overload, CLASS=HASH(0x..), HASH(0x..); a code ref too), nothing appended; an overload that dies prints THAT die's text.  cases 03/04 of the q5 battery: stderr + rc 255 = perl.
(b) THE AUDIT: 31 plain `(error "...")` sites whose text is a perldiag run-time fatal now raise through %p-die-error (89 -> 58 plain sites in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), and %p-die-error arms the uncaught hook as p-die does, so uncaught they are ONE line and exit 255.  Converted, by message: Not a/an ~A reference (1), Modification of a read-only value attempted (1), Can't take log of 0 / sqrt of ~A (2), Modification of non-creatable array value attempted (1), substr outside of string (1), Cannot chr ~A (2), Wide character in ~A (1), Integer overflow in format string (5), Assigned value is not a SCALAR/ARRAY/HASH/CODE reference (4), Not an ARRAY / Not a HASH reference (3), Operation "~A": no method found (1), Too few / Too many arguments for subroutine / Odd name/value argument (3), push on scalar forbidden / Type of arg 1 to push (2), Can't "continue"/"break" outside a when block (2), Can't find an opnumber (1), Attempt to bless into a reference (1).  The "Can't call method ..." sites were already p-die (quoted name).  The 58 remaining plain sites are internal invariants / host plumbing and stay LOUD, as the s494g brief ordered.  script: scratch/s494g/audit2108.pl.
Guard rows: Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t rows 14-18 (all five fail on 40da28bd); row 11 (#1427 boundary) rewritten to perl's 255.  ir-conform 022-refs left known-fail.tsv (Not a SCALAR reference exits 255 now).  ir-spec §7.5 "What an uncaught die PRINTS".
STILL OPEN (why this task stays pending): the USER s494 ruling's part (3) -- an INTERNAL error as one line `PCL internal error: <text> (set PCL_BACKTRACE=1 ...)`, with PCL_BACKTRACE set by tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm -- was explicitly NOT in s494g's brief.
subject: FAILURE EXPERIENCE: two everyday uncaught failures put Lisp in the user's face -- (a) an uncaught `die $ref` / `die $object` prints the BOX STRUCT (`#S(p-box :value #<hash-table ...> :nv nil ...`, 8 lines) where perl prints `HASH(0x...)` or the object's `""` overload text; (b) perl's own RUN-TIME FATALS raised inside the runtime as plain CL errors (`Can't call method "m" on an undefined value`, `Not a CODE reference`) reach the top level as "Unhandled simple-error in thread #<sb-thread:thread ...>" + a 30-line SBCL backtrace and EXIT 1, where perl prints one line and exits 255
